newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka extends refinery shutdown to 10-14 days.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka extends refinery shutdown to 10-14 days.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) will extend the shutdown of its 55,000-barrel per day (bpd) refinery to 10-14 days from the initial seven days, starting from June 1, a CPC official said on Thursday.
Earlier this week CPC's chairman Anil Obeyesekere said the unscheduled shutdown would be for about one week.
He said the shutdown was due to insufficient crude to run the refinery after CPC's single mooring buoy, which discharges crude from tankers to the refinery, was damaged in an accident last week.

The CPC official said the company has already lined up two to three tankers comprising combined cargoes of gas oil and jet fuel to compensate for a shortage in supplies ahead of the refinery shutdown.
CPC has allocated for imports of nearly 700,000 barrels of gas oil and 210,000 barrels of jet fuel for June, 30 percent more than its normal monthly requirements to make up for the shortage.
The official said that more might be required for end-June/early July if the shutdown were longer than expected.
